_: How the corner's trees are drawn, by habit: data for blender/parts/trees/corner.py (the build) and unity/Assets/Code/Editor/LT1CornerTrees.cs (the look). Style and species values only; the facts (where, when, how tall) are fixtures/lt1-corner.json and fixtures/lt1-corner-trees.json. Lengths in metres.

levels._: Each level's reach from the eye (m): near to 20 (the street stop and eye level), street to 60, far beyond (silhouettes in the air past 130 m are the far level's).

budget._: Triangles a level may draw (tools/check_trees.py): the near birch at the street stop, a far tree; each level at most share of the one before.

birch.masses_why: three to five masses (art direction, the trees); a downy birch's crown in four: its top, two over the lane and one over the yard
birch.shell_why: each mass drawn inside its foliage's fitted skin, so seams of sky open between masses
birch.seam_why: each mass moved this far out from the crown's middle, widening the seams
birch.shed_why: a downy birch sheds its shaded lower limbs (self-pruning, a pioneer that cannot bear shade): in a yard between houses its crown starts a third of its height up
birch.narrow_why: the downy birch's crown drawn narrower than grown, its limbs ascending (Oslo 19 Sep, ref 03)
birch.fallen_why: 20 October on the coast: a downy birch has dropped about a quarter of its leaves, the inner and low first
birch.lost_up_why: from this share of the crown's height up the masses thin (cards dropped up to the second value at the top) and take the thin card: the crown lost upward

spruce.crown_base_why: a planted garden spruce keeps its skirt to the ground
spruce.width_why: crown diameter at its foot as a share of the height (Norway spruce, open grown)
spruce.whorl_why: the whorls' spacing near the top and at the foot (m)
